} else if (field.type === 'attribute' && field.attribute) { item[field.name] = element.getAttribute(field.attribute); } ``` So: - `type: "url"` does nothing special; only `"text"` and `"attribute"` are supported for extraction. - To get `href`, you must: - Select the `` element (not the ``) via CSS or XPath - Use `type: "attribute"` - Set `attribute: "href"` ### Fixing your schema Assuming your row HTML looks like this: ```html Cell 1 Cell 2 Cell 3 View Download ``` Use `baseSelector: "tr"` (as you already do), then inside each `tr` use **CSS selectors** for the link elements and tell the schema to pull the `href` attribute: ```python pubs_schema = { "name": "news", "baseSelector": "tr", "fields": [ { "name": "Reference", "selector": "td:nth-child(1)", "type": "text", }, { "name": "Description", "selector": "td:nth-child(2)", "type": "text", }, { "name": "Date", "selector": "td:nth-child(3)", "type": "text", }, { "name": "View", "selector": "td:nth-child(4) a", # select the in 4th column "type": "attribute", "attribute": "href", }, { "name": "Download", "selector": "td:nth-child(5) a", # select the in 5th column "type": "attribute", "attribute": "href", }, ], } ``` Key points: - Use **CSS**, not XPath, for `selector` (your `"//tr/td[4]/a[/@href"` is invalid XPath *and* the engine here is using `querySelector`, not `evaluate`). - `"type": "attribute"` tells the extractor to call `element.getAttribute(field.attribute)` for that field. - `"attribute": "href"` specifies which attribute you want.
